key_insight: In routine memory-clinic practice, α-synuclein seed amplification assay (SAA) detected Lewy body pathology with high accuracy and identified α-synuclein co-pathology that standard Alzheimer fluid biomarkers largely missed.
clinical_relevance: SAA may be a useful complementary biomarker for improving diagnosis and patient stratification when Lewy body disease or mixed pathology is suspected.
method: 398 patients from a multicenter memory-clinic cohort were studied.
CSF and plasma Alzheimer biomarkers were measured alongside MMSE and clinician-confirmed diagnoses.
α-synuclein status was determined using RT-QuIC seed amplification assay.
evidence_signal: Among 20 Lewy body dementia cases, 95.0% were SAA-positive, and SAA showed 95.0% sensitivity and 93.1% specificity for distinguishing LBD from non-LBD/non-AD patients; within AD, most CSF and plasma biomarkers did not separate SAA+ from SAA- cases.
watch_item: This is a single cohort from memory-clinic practice, so broader performance and how best to integrate SAA into workflows still need external validation.
paper_title: Routine implementation of α-synuclein Seed Amplification Assays reveals high diagnostic performance and the limited value of Alzheimer disease fluid biomarkers for detecting α-synuclein co-pathology
